scope: Pennsylvania Governor and U.S. House, general election Nov 3 2026 (no U.S. Senate race)

angles.working_title: Pennsylvania governor: a 25-point Quinnipiac lead and a market near 0.98 for Shapiro
angles.interesting_fact: Quinnipiac's October 1-5 likely-voter poll had Gov. Josh Shapiro at 59% and Stacy Garrity at 34% (margin of error 3.9 points), and Kalshi's Democratic-party governor contract last traded at 0.984 on November 1.

sources.headline: Quinnipiac poll: Shapiro-Garrity race looks like a rout

angles.synopsis: Quinnipiac's October 7 release reports Shapiro at 59%, Garrity at 34%, Libertarian Ken Krawchuk at 2% and 4% undecided among 1,159 likely voters interviewed October 1 to 5 (margin of error 3.9 points including design effect). Shapiro's job approval was 63% to 30%. Quinnipiac says it is the first likely-voter poll of the cycle and cannot be compared with earlier registered-voter surveys (July: Shapiro 53%, Garrity 40%). The same poll found 54% to 39% favoring Democratic control of the U.S. House. Kalshi's governor event GOVPARTYPA-26, captured Nov 1 15:35 UTC, shows the Democratic-party contract at 0.984 last and the Republican-party contract at 0.022. A price is not a forecast. Neither governor candidate has a congressional record, so TIP shows all six issues Not graded.

angles.working_title: Pennsylvania's 1st: outside money arrives for Fitzpatrick, and two reports give different Congressional Leadership Fund figures
angles.interesting_fact: The Inquirer reported on October 16 that the Congressional Leadership Fund redirected $3.6 million to help Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick against Bob Harvie, while Jewish Insider reported on October 17 that the group put $4.5 million into the race that week.

sources.headline: Fitzpatrick, Harvie and campaign finance (Sam Janesch)
RJC drops $400,000 to boost Brian Fitzpatrick in Pennsylvania swing district

financial_claims.claim: CLF redirected $3.6 million to boost Fitzpatrick; the DCCC began a nearly $1 million campaign for Harvie that week
CLF put $4.5 million into the race this week, its first spending there since 2020; the RJC Victory Fund launched a $400,000 digital and streaming campaign
Harvie raised about $888,000 and spent $962,000 from July 1 to Sept. 30, with $721,000 on hand Oct. 1; Fitzpatrick spent $5 million over the summer, mostly on advertising, with $2.4 million on hand

angles.synopsis: The Inquirer (Oct 16) reports the Congressional Leadership Fund redirected $3.6 million to Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick in his race against Democrat Bob Harvie, the DCCC began a nearly $1 million campaign for Harvie, and Fitzpatrick spent $5 million over the summer while Harvie raised about $888,000. Jewish Insider (Oct 17) puts CLF spending at $4.5 million that week, its first in the district since 2020, and adds a $400,000 Republican Jewish Coalition digital buy; it calls the seat one of two that Kamala Harris won in 2024 and a Republican holds, rated lean Republican by Cook. The figures differ and neither outlet explains why, so both are given with attribution and not added. Kalshi's PA-01 event (HOUSEPA1-26), captured Nov 1 15:35 UTC, shows the Democratic-party contract at 0.53 last. Fitzpatrick has TIP grades (A+ Stock Trading Ban and Universal Healthcare; F- Data Bill of Rights, War-Crime Accountability and US-Israel Military Merger); Harvie is not graded.
unknowns: Why the CLF figures differ is not explained by either outlet
